note: Rewritten from the original description by Hill (1922); the original is in English. The species was placed in Hamitermes there and later transferred to Amitermes. The text is taken from the OCR of the BHL fascicle scan deposited in Zenodo (record 2333936); the original used an interpunct as the decimal point, which the OCR gives either as a hyphen or as "•", and these have been restored here to a decimal point according to the context.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Vertex, meso- and metathorax, legs, sternites and tergites all dark brown (mummy-brown), the pronotum a distinctly deeper brown; mouthparts earth-coloured; tarsi pale straw; claws pale rusty; wings brown. Head (fig. 13) sparsely covered with short hairs and hairs of moderate length, longer than wide, posterior margin and sides rounded, widest at the mandibular bases, vertex flat; frontal gland pore appearing as two fine, long, straight slits on the median line. Eyes small, hardly projecting beyond the sides of the head; ocelli oval, far from the eyes. Antennae 14-segmented, inserted on a raised tubercle within a deep, broad pit in front of the eyes, the tubercle lying about between the anterior margin of the eye and the posterior margin of the clypeus; segment 1 twice as long as segment 2, segment 3 the shortest, its limits from segments 2 and 4 indistinct. Labrum narrow at the base, inflated at the sides, anterior margin rounded. Anterior margin of the anteclypeus arched, slightly convex, half as long as wide, half as wide as the postclypeus, with a median suture continued onto the postclypeus. Postclypeus large, convex, anterior margin slightly concave, posterior margin semicircular, maximum length slightly greater than maximum width. Pronotum about twice as wide as long, anterior margin slightly convex and upturned, anterolateral corners rounded and slightly upturned, sides steeply sloping to the nearly straight posterior margin. Legs: fore tibia and all femora stout; tibial spur formula 3:2:2. Wings brown, the main veins and the first five or six branches of the cubitus distinct; ciliate all round except on the basal fifth of the posterior margin; a few long hairs along the full length of the veins, venation variable, the fore and hind wings of the same individual not always alike; transverse suture straight. Abdomen nearly cylindrical; sternite 7 of the male much longer and darker than the corresponding sternite of the female, densely covered with fine short red hairs; cerci short, conical, the basal segment very broad (0.8 mm) and flat. Measurements: body length with wings 6.25—7 mm; body length without wings 3.25—4 mm; head length with mandibles 0.75—0.84 mm; thorax and abdomen length 2.63 mm; head width with eyes 0.65—0.67 mm; antennal length 1.08 mm; mandible length/width: right 0.41/0.28 mm, left 0.4/0.25 mm; pronotum length 0.28 mm, width 0.51 mm; wing length 5 mm, width 1.27—1.4 mm; tibia length (fore/mid/hind) 0.51/0.48/0.7 mm.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head pale yellowish brown; antennae, maxillary palps, thorax and legs paler; abdomen grey (from the gut contents); mandibles chestnut brown, the basal half very pale. Head (fig. 15) rounded at the posterior margin and sides, flattened dorsoventrally, sparsely covered with short red hairs. Mandibles short and stout, each with an obtuse angular tooth in the middle. Labrum broad at the base, tapering to the rounded apex. Clypeus broad, its limits indistinct. Antennae inserted on a raised tubercle at the mandibular base, 13-segmented; segment 1 nearly twice as long as segment 2; segments 2 and 4 equal in length; segment 3 half the length of segments 2 and 4; segments 5 and 8 three quarters the length of segment 4; segments 9—11 equal in length to segment 2; segment 12 slightly longer; segment 13 the longest, twice as long as segments 2 and 4. Pronotum of the same shape as in the worker. Legs short and rather stout, tibial spur formula 3:2:2. Abdomen elongate-oval, with numerous hairs of moderate length and a few very long red hairs. Measurements: body length about 3.3 mm; head length with mandibles 1.22 mm; mandible length 0.47 mm; head width 0.65 mm, head thickness 0.47 mm; antennal length 0.86 mm; pronotum length 0.18 mm, width 0.47 mm; tibia length (fore/mid/hind) 0.46/0.37/0.56 mm; abdominal width 0.7 mm.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Head creamy white; mouthparts, thorax and legs paler; abdomen nearly transparent. Head nearly spherical, slightly longer than wide, sparsely covered with red hairs; labrum large and convex, anterior margin rounded; clypeus of the same shape as in the alate, with a rusty spot at each end (mandibular articulations). Antennae 13-segmented, segmentation as in the alate, inserted on a raised tubercle. Tooth pattern as in the alate. Pronotum about twice as wide as long, anterior part arched and upturned. Legs stout, tibial spur formula 3:2:2. Abdomen elongate-oval, apex bluntly rounded, with hairs of moderate length and thickness and, in addition, a few very long hairs on the dorsal and ventral surfaces; cerci large and conspicuous, with several very long fine hairs at the base. Measurements: body length about 3.47 mm; head length with mandibles 0.7 mm; thorax and abdomen length 2.68 mm; head width 0.64 mm, head thickness 0.32 mm; antennal length 0.98 mm; mandible length/width: left 0.38/0.25 mm, right 0.36/0.28 mm; pronotum length 0.22 mm, width 0.4 mm; tibia length (fore/mid/hind) 0.46/0.38/0.56 mm.

sections.label: Other
sections.text: The small size of the soldier separates it at once from the known Australian species of Hamitermes; the closest species is A. latidens, from which it differs in its smaller size and in the number and shape of the antennal segments. Type locality: Townsville, northern Queensland; alates, soldiers and workers were taken in garden soil heavily dressed with stable manure on 10 and 18 December (month 12) 1919, and after about 50 points of rain on the night of 17 December, alates were seen flying from sandy soil the next morning.
